questions.question: How should a rider sit to best control a motorcycle?

options.text: Using arms to hold the body up.
With knees away from the gas tank.
With feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: With feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support your body. Your arms should be slightly bent on the handgrips. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: What should you do if another driver is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What happens to steering if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: There will be no change in the steering.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, exit the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: Where should you look when turning on a motorcycle?

options.text: Close to the front of the motorcycle.
Through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.
Increase your speed before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which action should you NOT take to stay safe when riding at night?

options.text: Use your high beam headlight when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when not near other vehicles, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead—their headlights help you see the road, and their taillights show if the road is bumpy.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective gear for motorcycle riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, footwear that covers and supports your ankles, and hearing protection.

questions.question: How do you make a motorcycle lean into a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip opposite the turn direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make this happen.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: About three-quarters
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It supplies about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Which protects your face best while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: What can a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protect a rider's face in a crash.
Should never be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also protects you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after the engine has been started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine has been started.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you leave. Tell them to get on the motorcycle only after you start the engine. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. Riding a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: You should not check before riding.
You should only check after riding.
It can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: How should you adjust your riding when carrying a passenger?

options.text: Follow other vehicles more closely than usual.
Brake a little later than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger means your motorcycle needs more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Reduce your speed, start slowing earlier than normal, increase your following distance, and look for larger gaps when entering or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What is the horn useful for on a motorcycle?

options.text: Other drivers usually cannot hear it.
It can get someone's attention quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help you get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Do not rely only on your horn to handle a hazard.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position for riding?

options.text: You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the handgrips.
Your knees are away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Do not stretch to reach them. Keep your knees against the gas tank to maintain balance.

questions.question: If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four drinks
questions.explanation: The body eliminates about one drink per hour. Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals about four drinks remaining.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wearing bright colors and reflective materials increases your visibility at all times.

questions.question: What does eye contact from a driver mean?

options.text: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
They will always yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look at motorcyclists but fail to consciously notice them.
